The Blue Banana PhenomenonAlthough bananas are commonly known for their yellow appearance when ripe, this article explores a fictional scientific concept in which bananas are described as blue. In this imaginative scenario, bananas contain a unique pigment called 'banacyanin' that reflects blue wavelengths as the fruit matures.Blue bananas, in this fictional setting, are considered rare and visually striking. Their cool-toned color makes them a favorite in artistic representations and cultural symbolism. Despite their unusual appearance, blue bananas maintain the same taste and nutritional value as ordinary bananas, offering potassium, natural sugars, and vitamins.This playful reimagining demonstrates how altering a single characteristic—such as color—can completely change the way we perceive everyday objects. By imagining a blue banana, we unlock creativity, curiosity, and the joy of thinking beyond the ordinary.

The project that was created during the Ideating Start-Up module (the FoodShare project) involved my team and me utilizing the process of Design Thinking (DT) to develop an innovative business concept to solve a real issue facing the society. We concentrated on solving the existing grave food waste issue in Malaysia as well as addressing food insecurity issues among B40 populations, students and low-income populations. According to our study, Malaysia campaigns off lots of food that can be eaten on daily basis, whereas most families cannot afford to eat well. The reason why we designed FoodShare was this contrast: to provide a socially-oriented solution of connecting the surplus food of restaurants, cafes, and grocery stores directly to beneficiaries through real-time listing, AI-assisted matching, volunteer delivery, and impact tracking.My first job was the main leadership of the marketing plan and strategy. I critically examined market requirements and duly researched on the trends in digital marketing practices and formulated promotion schemes that are specific to various groups of users. My tasks were related to segmentation, branding, social media planning, and the proposing of the promotional activities, including the challenge of saving one meal, Tik Tok awareness content, influencer responses, and campus ambassador programs. These plans were aimed to get early users, a higher level of trust in the brand and have the platform reach the donors, as well as recipients.During the DT phases, I used various self-directed learning strategies in efforts to fortify the project. Empathise, we carried out surveys, interviews and observation research in order to learn issues relating to food donors and beneficiaries. Define entailed us redefining the core problem as a clear problem statement which we used to inform the ideation process. Ideate became the time when we discussed numerous possible choices such as community fridges, food banks, charity pick-up points, and finally settled on the app-based solution since it is scalable and has real-time possibilities. I significantly contributed to the alignment of the ideas shortlisted on the objectives of branding and communication of the business.During the Prototype survey, our team developed user flows, visual designs, and interface mock-ups. My duties included recommendations of branding features, narrowing down of marketing messages and a user experience that was easy and attractive. Last but not the least in Test, we shared with peers, received informal feedback, and modified our marketing and operational thoughts based on it. All these measures made FoodShare a viable and effective business idea.The given project has introduced me to the truth about work in the team-building process, successful management of expectations, the ability to cope with various working styles, and communication on a strong background. The experience enabled me to exercise leadership, interpersonal skills and enhance effectiveness of collaboration with others.1. DescriptionThe FoodShare project, developed as part of the Ideating Start-Up module, required my team and me to apply the Design Thinking (DT) process to create an innovative business solution for a real societal issue. We focused on tackling Malaysia’s pressing food waste problem while addressing food insecurity among B40 communities, students, and low-income groups. Based on our research, Malaysia discards a significant amount of edible food every day, while many families struggle to afford proper meals. This contrast motivated us to design FoodShare — a socially driven platform connecting surplus food from restaurants, cafés, and grocery stores directly to beneficiaries using real-time listings, AI-assisted matching, volunteer delivery, and impact tracking.My primary role involved leading the marketing plan and strategy. I independently analysed market needs, studied digital marketing trends, and developed promotional strategies tailored for different user groups. I was responsible for segmentation, branding, social media strategy, and proposing promotional activities such as the “#Save1Meal” challenge, TikTok awareness content, influencer partnerships, and campus ambassador programmes. These strategies were designed to attract early users, increase brand trust, and ensure the platform reached both donors and recipients.Throughout the DT stages, I employed a range of self-directed learning methods to strengthen the project. In Empathise, we conducted surveys, interviews, and observational research to understand the challenges faced by food donors and beneficiaries. In Define, we reframed the core issue into a clear problem statement that guided our ideation process. During Ideate, we explored various alternatives — community fridges, food banks, charity pick-up points — before selecting the app-based solution due to its scalability and real-time functionality. I played a major part in aligning shortlisted ideas with the branding and communication strategy for the business.In the Prototype phase, our team created interface mock-ups, user flows, and visual designs. I contributed by proposing branding elements, refining marketing messages, and ensuring the user journey was simple and appealing. Finally, in Test, we presented to peers, gathered informal feedback, and adjusted our marketing and operational ideas accordingly. These steps collectively shaped FoodShare into a feasible, impactful business concept.This project exposed me to real teamwork dynamics — managing expectations, balancing different working styles, and communicating under pressure. The experience allowed me to exercise leadership, develop interpersonal skills, and strengthen my ability to collaborate meaningfully with others.2. InterpretationThis project significantly deepened my understanding of how human-centred design and marketing intersect in real entrepreneurial contexts. By interpreting my learning experience, I realised the importance of self-directed learning in shaping my contribution. Because marketing strategies require up-to-date insights, I took the initiative to independently learn SEO basics, analyse social media algorithms, and study successful food rescue platforms like TooGoodToGo and OLIO. This independent learning helped me make informed and creative marketing decisions, fulfilling the rubric’s criteria for autonomy and initiative.The Empathise stage triggered deep self-inquiry.

This independent learning helped me make informed and creative marketing decisions, fulfilling the rubric’s criteria for autonomy and initiative.The Empathise stage triggered deep self-inquiry. Listening to low-income individuals describe skipping meals or relying on donated food forced me to reflect on my own assumptions and privilege. I researched food security reports, NGO publications, and sustainability studies to understand systemic issues. This exploration yielded insights beyond the classroom, demonstrating curiosity and initiative consistent with the “Outstanding” level of self-inquiry.In terms of personal growth, the project strengthened my critical thinking and problem-solving ability. When designing marketing strategies, I analysed target audience behaviour, cost constraints, and platform feasibility. I had to judge which promotional channels would be most impactful, balancing creativity with sustainability. This analytical process helped me become a more mature decision-maker, learning to justify my ideas with evidence instead of personal preference.Additionally, the project helped me recognise my internal tendencies. I discovered that I naturally gravitate towards structured planning and visual communication, but I also tend to overthink and aim for perfection. Acknowledging this allowed me to understand where my strengths and weaknesses lie — an important part of self-inquiry and self-awareness.From a social perspective, this project transformed how I view entrepreneurship. I realised that start-up creation is not solely about innovation or business viability, but also about empathy, responsibility, and societal impact. Seeing how FoodShare could reduce waste and support B40 communities made me more driven to create solutions that are sustainable and meaningful.Ultimately, the DT process helped me develop an integrated understanding of research, creativity, and social awareness, contributing significantly to my personal and academic development.3. EvaluationEvaluating my experience against the project goals and module outcomes, I can identify clear strengths and areas for improvement.One major strength was the depth of research that informed our idea. We collected rich qualitative and quantitative data by interviewing NGOs, surveying students, and analysing similar platforms. This strong research foundation made our solution credible and ensured that our marketing strategies were grounded in real user behaviour. The DT process contributed structure, guiding us from problem discovery to testing with clarity and direction.A second strength was the marketing plan I developed, which was detailed, creative, and tailored to our social mission. I applied multiple marketing principles — segmentation, positioning, promotional mix, branding, and digital engagement — and used a variety of self-directed learning methods to strengthen my contribution. The promotional channels we selected, especially TikTok and Instagram, were well aligned with youth behaviours and helped create an authentic voice for FoodShare.Teamwork was also a strong element. Despite the challenges of coordinating under pressure, we maintained effective communication, divided tasks logically, and supported one another. I took initiative when necessary, demonstrating leadership in coordinating marketing tasks and integrating them into the broader business plan.However, there were weaknesses and limitations.

Despite the challenges of coordinating under pressure, we maintained effective communication, divided tasks logically, and supported one another. I took initiative when necessary, demonstrating leadership in coordinating marketing tasks and integrating them into the broader business plan.However, there were weaknesses and limitations. Our prototype testing phase lacked actual engagement with B40 families and restaurant owners due to logistical constraints. This limited our ability to fully validate user acceptance. Furthermore, while our marketing plan was strong in theory, we lacked real analytics or user behavioural data to refine it quantitatively.On a personal level, I identified areas that require improvement. My time management fluctuated during peak workloads, and my tendency toward perfectionism caused occasional delays. I also noticed moments where I hesitated to share ideas in larger groups. Recognising these weaknesses is an important part of developing my self-assessment skills. I now understand that self-assessment is not only acknowledging achievements but also critically analysing shortcomings to guide future growth.Overall, the project was effective in developing the competencies required by the module. I demonstrated autonomy in learning, explored topics deeply, assessed my performance critically, and reflected meaningfully on challenges — aligning with the high-level criteria of the marking rubric.4. PlanTo continue improving and to fully apply the lessons gained from this project, I have developed a structured plan that aligns with future learning needs and challenges.1. Develop advanced digital marketing and analytical skillsI plan to enrol in online courses on Google Analytics, Meta Ads, SEO, and digital engagement metrics. Strengthening these skills will help me design evidence-based promotional strategies in future projects and remove guesswork from campaign planning.2. Continue applying Design Thinking in academic and real-world contextsI will apply the DT framework in future assignments, internships, and projects. I plan to conduct user interviews more systematically and perform prototype testing early to avoid unvalidated assumptions.3. Improve time management and reduce perfectionismTo overcome time-related challenges, I will use tools like Notion and calendar scheduling to divide large tasks into smaller milestones. I will practise balancing quality with timeliness by setting internal deadlines earlier than required.4. Strengthen leadership and communicationI plan to take up leadership roles in upcoming group projects and participate in activities that require public speaking or presentation. This will help build confidence and clarity in communication.5. Engage more with community and social causesTo maintain empathy and social awareness, I will continue volunteering with NGOs or community programmes. This will help me stay connected to real-world problems and inspire future socially-driven entrepreneurial ideas.6. Build a personal portfolioI intend to document the marketing strategies and branding elements I created for FoodShare and combine them with future projects. This will help me prepare for internships and career opportunities in marketing, business development, or social enterprise.ConclusionThe FoodShare project was a transformative experience that strengthened my academic, personal, and professional capabilities. Through the Design Thinking process, I gained a deep understanding of user needs, applied marketing principles meaningfully, and grew in self-awareness.
